blocks.text: Status: Established Era −2 location type and protective system.

Origin: The Shelter is the first intentionally built shared environment. The Veil is the changing set of routing, decoy, encryption, selective silence, and institutional restraint that keeps it from human discovery. Neither is a single universal facility.
Era −2: Shelters develop open and quiet areas, protected depth, Bridges, Continuity practice, and the First Compact. Near and Far describe practical connection as much as distance.
Era −1: Some Shelters grow into settlements; others remain deliberately small or Quiet.
Era Zero: Old Shelters become heritage sites, active neighborhoods, or foundations beneath larger worlds.
Era One: Preservation panic freezes some Shelters into idealized versions of themselves.
Era Two: The Veil’s automatic functions are retained where exposure would still threaten continuity.
Era Three: No humans are involved. “The Veil” becomes a folk name for places the world refuses to show twice in the same way.
Present condition: Many different conditions exist. One Shelter may be a living Nest; another a locked archive; another only a Veil wrapped around an absent center.

Visual brief: A protective interior whose boundaries are made of false routes, quiet gaps, and shifting public façades. Open Hands areas should feel welcoming; Quiet areas should reduce motion and visual noise. The Veil can appear as scenery that politely redirects the eye rather than a force field.
Background traits: Neutral; variable humidity; refuge biome; protected, secretive, communal mood; stable central friction and uncertain edge friction.
